header.one_liner: Series of ~500-tonne self-propelled fuel barges ordered for the Indian Navy to sustain fleet bunkering at coastal bases; built under a Make-in-India shipbuilding programme (CSL/GRSE and private yards).

what_it_is.prose: The 500t self-propelled fuel barges are a series of small bunkering vessels built for the Indian Navy to deliver fuel oil and diesel to warships at anchorage and at naval bases — a low-profile but operationally vital part of the fleet logistics chain. Naval fuel barges keep surface combatants bunkered without tying up main berths or requiring large tankers, sustaining readiness across the Navy's coastal commands and forward bases. The programme was pursued as a Make-in-India shipbuilding acquisition, with the Indian Navy ordering a series of 500-tonne-class self-propelled fuel barges built at domestic yards (including state-owned Cochin Shipyard Limited / GRSE and qualifying private yards), reflecting the Navy's push to build even logistics craft indigenously. Each barge carries on the order of 500 tonnes of liquid fuel (diesel/oil), is self-propelled (with a modest engine for harbour and short coastal transits), and is crewed by a small naval or civilian crew. While individually unremarkable, the craft are strategically important because they keep India's surface fleet — including the P17A frigates and carriers — supplied with fuel at distributed bases, and they test the Indian civilian shipbuilding base's ability to meet naval-spec requirements at modest size.

deployments_procurement.summary: The Indian Navy placed contract(s) for a series of 500t self-propelled fuel barges under a Make-in-India acquisition. Exact quantities, per-vessel cost and delivery schedule are not fully public — the programme is flagged with uncertainty on precise numbers, though it forms part of the Navy's broader programme of building support and auxiliary craft (fuel barges, water barges, tugs and ferries) at Indian yards.

faq.question: What are the 500t self-propelled fuel barges used for?
faq.answer: They are small bunkering craft that deliver fuel oil and diesel to Indian Navy warships at anchorage and naval bases, keeping the surface fleet supplied without tying up main berths or deploying large tankers.

faq.question: Are the fuel barges built in India?
faq.answer: Yes. The 500t fuel barges are built at Indian shipyards (including CSL/GRSE and private yards) under a Make-in-India acquisition, though some engines and fuel-handling equipment retain import content.

faq.question: Why do such small craft matter strategically?
faq.answer: Distributed fuel supply keeps India's surface fleet — including P17A frigates and carriers — ready at forward and coastal bases. Building even logistics craft indigenously also strengthens the Indian civilian shipbuilding base against naval specifications.
